title: Advanced Prototyping and Prototype Testing
summary: This lesson covers digital interface prototyping, comparing low-fidelity and high-fidelity prototypes, using Figma and Adobe XD, designing interactive user flows, and conducting prototype testing and usability evaluations.

sections.title: Introduction to Prototyping
paragraphs: Prototyping is the process of creating an early model or representation of a website, mobile application, or software before developing the actual product.
It allows designers to test the layout, features, navigation, and interactions before implementation.
list: Improves communication between designers and developers.
Reduces development costs and unnecessary revisions.

sections.title: Low-Fidelity Prototype
paragraphs: A simple representation of an interface.
Example: A hand-drawn sketch of a login page.

sections.title: High-Fidelity Prototype
paragraphs: A detailed and interactive representation of the proposed interface.
Example: A clickable mobile banking application prototype.

sections.title: Low-Fidelity vs. High-Fidelity Prototypes
list: Low-Fidelity: Simple design, basic shapes and sketches, limited interaction, faster to create, focuses on structure, used in early design stages.
High-Fidelity: Detailed design, realistic interface elements, interactive features, requires more time, focuses on appearance and behavior, used for detailed evaluation.

sections.title: What is Figma?
paragraphs: Figma is a cloud-based design and prototyping tool used to create websites, mobile applications, and user interfaces.

sections.title: Important Features in Figma
list: Frames: Used to represent screens or pages of a design. Example: Login Screen, Home Screen, and Profile Screen.
Layers: Used to organize individual design elements. Example: Text, images, buttons, and icons.
Components: Reusable design elements that maintain consistency. Example: A navigation bar used across multiple screens.
Auto Layout: Automatically organizes and adjusts elements based on their content and spacing.
Prototyping: Connects screens and creates interactive user flows.

sections.title: What is Adobe XD?
paragraphs: Adobe XD is a user experience design tool developed by Adobe for creating website and mobile application interfaces.
Adobe XD is no longer actively developed with new features and is in maintenance mode.
Figma is a practical primary choice for new classroom prototyping projects, while Adobe XD can still be discussed and used where it is available.

sections.title: What is Interactive Prototyping?
paragraphs: Interactive prototyping is the process of connecting different screens and adding actions to simulate how a real application works.
list: Clicking a button to open another screen.

sections.title: Understanding User Flow
paragraphs: A user flow represents the steps a user follows to complete a specific task in an application.
A good user flow should be simple, logical, and easy to follow.
A prototype does not necessarily need a working database, backend, or actual login authentication. Its primary purpose is to demonstrate the proposed interface and user interactions.

sections.title: What is Prototype Testing?
paragraphs: Prototype testing is the process of evaluating a prototype by allowing users to interact with it and perform specific tasks. It helps designers determine whether the design meets user requirements before actual development.

sections.title: Methods of Prototype Testing
list: Task-Based Testing: Users perform specific tasks using the prototype.
Think-Aloud Testing: Users explain their thoughts while interacting with the prototype.
Observation: The researcher watches how users interact with the prototype.
User Interviews: Ask participants about their experience after testing.
Questionnaire or Survey: Collect ratings and suggestions about the prototype.

sections.title: Comprehensive Usability Evaluation
paragraphs: A comprehensive usability evaluation examines different aspects of the prototype.
list: Functionality: Do the buttons and interactions work as intended?
Navigation: Can users easily move between screens?
Visual Design: Is the interface organized and attractive?
Usability: Can users complete tasks without difficulty?
Accessibility: Can different users access and understand the interface?
Consistency: Are the design elements consistent across screens?
User Satisfaction: Are users satisfied with the experience?

sections.title: Improving a Prototype Based on Feedback
paragraphs: After testing, designers should improve the prototype based on user feedback.
A prototype is not the final product. It should be continuously evaluated and improved based on user feedback.
list: User Feedback: Login button is difficult to find. -> Design Improvement: Make the button more visible.
User Feedback: Text is too small. -> Design Improvement: Increase font size.
User Feedback: Navigation is confusing. -> Design Improvement: Simplify the menu.
User Feedback: Too many steps to enroll. -> Design Improvement: Reduce unnecessary steps.
User Feedback: Users cannot identify icons. -> Design Improvement: Add text labels.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
list: Prototyping allows designers to visualize and test an application before development.
Low-fidelity prototypes focus on basic structure.
High-fidelity prototypes simulate the actual interface and interactions.
Figma and Adobe XD are tools used for interface design and prototyping.
Interactive prototypes demonstrate how users navigate through an application.
Prototype testing identifies usability issues and helps improve the final design.
